skill.name: router
skill.description: Routes any game-development request to the right specialized skill(s): it detects the engine (Godot, Unity, Unreal, Ebitengine, Bevy, Phaser, PixiJS, three.js, Defold, LÖVE, pygame, Roblox) and the task, then reads the chosen skill before acting. Use to make a game or to decide which skill applies — for players, levels, enemies, shaders, art direction, sprites, tiles, textures, 3D assets, UI/UX, cameras, game feel, physics, input, audio, saving, multiplayer, AI, dialogue, procedural generation, or performance, for genres (platformer, roguelike, RPG, FPS, tower-defense, card game, visual novel, survival-crafting, puzzle), and for shipping (game jam, Steam, itch). Start here when unsure which gamedev skill to use.
skill.summary: Selects focused game-development skills from engine evidence, project versions, and task requirements.
skill.author: gamedev-skills

security_audit.summary: All 128 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, ordinary prose, and game-development terminology. Context confirms routing guidance rather than shell execution, scope manipulation, or host and network reconnaissance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed files.

content.user_title: Route Game Development Tasks to Focused Skills
content.value_statement: Game-development requests can span engines, mechanics, and publishing workflows, making skill selection difficult. This router uses project evidence and task keywords to select focused skills.
actual_capabilities: Identifies twelve game-engine families from project files, dependency metadata, imports, or explicit engine names.
Directs version checks to project metadata and lockfiles before choosing version-sensitive APIs.
Maps requests to engine skills, cross-engine disciplines, genre templates, and publishing workflows.
Selects minimal skill combinations and defines their responsibilities and loading order.
Limits document loading to selected skill bodies and task-relevant references.
Preserves custom engines and identifies missing bindings instead of inventing APIs or skill names.
limitations: Provides routing instructions, not engine implementations, executable tooling, or complete games.
Requires access to separately available specialized skills for the selected tasks.
Some engines lack dedicated movement, tilemap, UI, or physics skills.
Cannot verify proprietary APIs without project documentation, source, SDK declarations, or working examples.

use_cases.title: Find Skills for a First Game Feature
use_cases.description: Select movement and genre skills for a Godot platformer without loading unrelated engine material.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Focused Debugging
use_cases.description: Route Unity performance or Roblox UI issues to the relevant engine and discipline skills while preserving project versions.

use_cases.title: Integrate Concepts into Custom Engines
use_cases.description: Map portable inventory and persistence concepts onto verified project APIs without replacing the existing engine.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Skills for a Simple Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use router to choose the smallest skill set for adding a double jump to my Godot player. Explain each choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a named engine and one gameplay feature.

prompt_templates.title: Detect the Project Engine
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my target project and identify its engine and pinned version. Route a HUD scaling issue to the relevant skills without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: project-based detection and focused UI routing.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a Genre Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Route a procedural dungeon roguelike task for my existing Godot project. Select minimal engine, generation, and genre skills, and explain their loading order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combining engine, discipline, and genre concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Bind Skills to a Proprietary Engine
prompt_templates.prompt: Route inventory and persistence work for our proprietary C++ engine. Preserve its toolchain, identify required API evidence, and state unknown bindings before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evidence-based integration with an unsupported engine.

output_examples.input: Add a double jump to my Godot player.
output: Engine: Godot, explicitly named in the request.
Selected skills: godot-2d-movement, followed by platformer.
Reason: movement guidance covers the controller; platformer guidance covers jump behavior and feel.

output_examples.input: How should I design save slots with migration?
output: Engine: not required for this conceptual question.
Reason: persistence structure and migration are portable concerns; engine bindings can be selected later.

output_examples.input: Add an inventory to our proprietary C++ RPG.
output: Engine: retain the existing proprietary engine.
Selected guidance: custom-engine reference, rpg, and save-systems.
Required evidence: content definitions, player-state ownership, UI events, and the existing serializer.
Unknown API bindings remain explicit until project evidence establishes them.

best_practices: Identify the target subproject and inspect its engine version before selecting engine-specific APIs.
Load only selected skill bodies, then open references when the current task requires them.
Preserve existing engines and versions, and state missing skills or unverified API bindings.
anti_patterns: Loading every engine and genre skill for a narrow request.
Replacing an existing custom engine with Godot because the catalog lacks an exact match.
Treating genre examples as verified APIs or inventing unavailable skill names.

faq.question: Does this skill build games by itself?
faq.answer: No. It selects specialized skills and their loading order; implementation depends on those skills and the project environment.

faq.question: Which engines can it identify?
faq.answer: It lists Godot, Unity, Unreal, Ebitengine, Bevy, Phaser, PixiJS, three.js, Defold, LÖVE, pygame, and Roblox.

faq.question: Are the specialized skills included?
faq.answer: This bundle contains routing instructions and references, not the specialized engine, discipline, genre, or publishing skills.

faq.question: What happens when the engine is unknown?
faq.answer: Conceptual tasks can proceed without an engine. Blocking ambiguity prompts one question; only new projects without a preference default to Godot.

faq.question: Can it support a proprietary engine?
faq.answer: It preserves the engine and maps portable concepts onto verified local APIs. Missing documentation or declarations remain explicit limitations.

faq.question: When should I run the router again?
faq.answer: Run it when the task changes engine or concern. Continue using the selected skill while the task remains within its scope.
